notes.subject: other
notes.text: Traffic drives on the left, shared in Europe only with Ireland, Malta and Cyprus.

notes.subject: plate
notes.text: White front plates and yellow rear plates; many lack the blue strip. Newer electric cars may have a green strip.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Double yellow lines along road edges, mostly in towns, mark no-stopping zones.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Centre lines of long dashes with reflective cat's eyes in the gaps are a good hint.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: Rounded bollard with black base and top, a white middle stripe, a red front reflector and a white rear one.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: A yellow traffic bollard is also commonly seen.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Wooden poles with thin horizontal metal rods bolted on as steps; sometimes a metal crossbar with two diagonal braces.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Yellow warning stickers on poles show a person being zapped by lightning; the neighbour's lack the person.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Chevrons are black with white arrows.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Warning signs are red-bordered white triangles; Ireland uses yellow diamonds.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Direction signs may be blue, green or white, with road numbers starting A, M or B.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: White street signs with black text set low on two small posts, often with a cul-de-sac icon in suburbs.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Yield signs carry the phrase GIVE WAY; Ireland's say YIELD.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Crossings are marked by black and white striped poles topped by a yellow globe; crossing signs are almost absent.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Rural metal gates have square corners; those in Ireland and Northern Ireland are rounded.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Very green with hedgerows lining roads and low rolling hills; Ireland looks very similar.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Terraced and semi-detached houses are very common, with 61% of people living in them.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Red brick is common in many parts, as in the Netherlands, Belgium and Denmark.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Suburbs have near-identical semi-detached houses with tidy lawns and maze-like cul-de-sac layouts.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Chimneys topped with multiple round, brick-coloured chimney pots.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Black-and-white timber framing on old and new buildings; less common in Ireland.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: The first digit of A and B road numbers groups regions, such as 3 for the southwest.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: All of Northern Ireland uses code 028 and the capital 020; other area codes follow no clear geographic order.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Semi-barren, very mountainous scenery, often brown and yellow in spring coverage.

notes.subject: bollard
notes.text: Bulky round red-and-white bollard whose red-and-grey reflector wraps fully round; the French one is more pointed.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Diamond-shaped Passing Place signs are most common in Scotland.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Celtic language with many D, W and Y and a distinct double LL. Road signs are bilingual in Wales.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Road markings in two languages, like Araf for Slow, appear only in Wales.

notes.subject: language
notes.text: Scottish Gaelic uses clusters like bh, dh, fh, mh and accents; green or yellow text on signs, mostly north of Glasgow.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Houses of big sandstone or granite blocks: granite in Aberdeen, red sandstone in Glasgow, yellow in Edinburgh.

notes.subject: vegetation
notes.text: Cordyline palms are most common along the far southwest coast and in Jersey.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Warning stickers wrapped fully around utility poles are specific to Northern Ireland.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Very hilly with exposed rocks and stone walls; rockier than the Scottish Highlands.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Street signs show the name in black followed by postcode and borough in red.
